text:
mike chan: FYI — audit shows ~30 KMS Decrypt calls from svc-analytics@infra (acct 222222222) against alias/customer-data-key since 02:15 UTC, right after the role-consolidation deploy.
ana patel: link to logs: https://logs.internal/replay?query=kms+Decrypt+alias/customer-data-key
jordan lee: severity? does this look like legit analytics traffic or an escalation?
mike chan: looks unexpected — those calls were previously limited to svc-processor. The consolidated role mapping added a principal group and I think a wildcard slipped into the key policy.
sec-bot: ALERT: unusual_kms_decrypt_rate for alias/customer-data-key (anomaly score 8.7)
deploy-bot: rolled deploy 2026-03-20T02:12Z (role-consolidation) to prod
ana patel: grabbing current key policy now, will paste snippet
ana patel: ```{\n  "Statement": [\n    {\n      "Effect": "Allow",\n      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222:role/service-role/*"},\n      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt"],\n      "Resource": "*"\n    }\n  ]\n}```
jordan lee: oof — that Principal pattern is too broad. We only wanted svc-processor and svc-archiver roles.
mike chan: mitigation suggestion: 1) add explicit Deny for arn:aws:iam::222222222:role/service-role/* on kms:Decrypt 2) revert role-consolidation mapping 3) rotate the CMK if there's any risk of exported plaintext
sre-oncall: we should avoid rotating key unless we have to — rekeying will impact lots of consumers. can we scope the policy first and monitor?
ana patel: applying a temporary key policy patch to deny decrypts from the analytics account principal and restricting Allow to explicit roles.
ana patel: running:
```bash
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id alias/customer-data-key --policy file://tmp-deny-2222.json --profile infra-admin
``` 
deploy-bot: policy update job queued (job-id j-9a8b)
sec-bot: INFO: blocked 12 decrypt calls since policy patch applied
mike chan: good. Jordan, can you roll back the role-consolidation PR in prod mapping? That should stop new principals from being granted.
jordan lee: rolling mapping back now, ETA 3m
jordan lee: done — mapping reverted. verifying service identities.
ana patel: forensic checklist started: collecting CloudTrail events, KMS event logs, which principals called decrypt, and timestamps. dumping into /tmp/kms_forensic_1878001234.log
mike chan: ping @sre-oncall on throttles — any downstream errors from denied decrypts?
 sre-oncall: seeing ~45 401-like errors from svc-analytics; not customer-facing but causes job failures. We should route retries to dead-letter and notify owners.
jordan lee: created incident ticket SEC-1221 and page to infra-analytics owners
ana patel: after patch, policy now explicitly allows only:
- arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/svc-processor
- arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/svc-archiver
and denies arn:aws:iam::222222222:role/service-role/* for kms:Decrypt
mike chan: next steps: ANA -> finish forensic & confirm no exports, JORDAN -> confirm rollback propagation and coordinate with analytics team, MIKE -> prepare customer-risk assessment and comms stub
ana patel: ETA 2h for forensic summary
jordan lee: ETA 30m to validate role mapping and perms across accounts
sec-bot: REMINDER: run key rotation assessment if any evidence of key material exposure is found
mike chan: thanks all. keep this thread for updates. :thumbsup:
